Q 43:26–28 · Vol. 4, p. 246

Verses 26 to 28

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people, “Indeed, I am disassociated from what you worship (26) except for He who created me, for indeed He will guide me” (27) And he made it a word remaining among his descendants, that perhaps they would return (28)
وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَراءٌ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ (26) إِلاَّ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ (27) وَجَعَلَها كَلِمَةً باقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (28)
Vol. 4, p. 246
It is read “barāʾ” with fatḥa on the bāʾ and with ḍamma; and “barīʾ.” “Barīʾ” and “barāʾ” are like “karīm” and “karām,”(1) and “barāʾ” is a verbal noun like “ẓamāʾ,” and for that reason the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine, are alike in it. One says: “We are barāʾ from you” and “khalāʾ from you.” “Except for He who created me”: it has more than one aspect: that it be accusative as a disconnected exception, as if he said: “but He who created me — for indeed He will guide me”; or that it be genitive as a substitute for what is governed by “min,” as if he said: “Indeed I am disassociated from what you worship except from Him who created me.”
قرئ: براء، بفتح الباء وضمها. وبريء، فبرىء وبراء، نحو كريم وكرام، «1» وبراء: مصدر كظماء، ولذلك استوى فيه الواحد والاثنان والجماعة، والمذكر والمؤنث. يقال: نحن البراء منك، والخلاء منك الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فيه غير وجه: أن يكون منصوبا على أنه استثناء منقطع، كأنه قال: لكن الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين، وأن يكون مجرورا بدلا من المجرور بمن، كأنه قال: إننى براء مما تعبدون إلا من الذي فطرني.
Question
If you say: how do you make it a substitute when it is not of the kind of what they worship, for two reasons: one, that God’s Essence differs from all essences, so it differs from the essences of what they worship; and two, that God Most High was not worshipped among them while the idols were worshipped?
فإن قلت: كيف تجعله بدلا وليس من جنس ما يعبدون من وجهين، أحدهما: أن ذات الله مخالفة لجميع الذوات، فكانت مخالفة لذوات ما يعبدون. والثاني، أن الله تعالى غير معبود بينهم والأوثان معبودة؟
Answer
I say: they said: they used to worship God along with their idols; or that “illā” be an adjective in the sense of “ghayr,” on the basis that “mā” in “mā taʿbudūn” is qualified [indefinite], its estimate being: “Indeed I am disassociated from gods you worship other than Him who created me”; so it parallels His saying Most High “Had there been in them [the heavens and earth] gods besides God, they would have been ruined.”
قلت: قالوا: كانوا يعبدون الله مع أوثانهم، وأن تكون إِلَّا صفة بمعنى غير، على أن «ما» في ما تعبدون موصوفة، تقديره: إننى براء من آلهة تعبدونها غير الذي فطرني، فهو نظير قوله تعالى لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا.
Question
If you say: what is the meaning of His saying “sa-yahdīn” [“He will guide me”] — as postponement?
فإن قلت: ما معنى قوله سَيَهْدِينِ على التسويف؟
Answer
I say: he said once “fa-huwa yahdīn” [“and He guides me”] and another time “fa-innahu sa-yahdīn”; so combine the two and estimate it as though he said: “He guides me and will guide me,” so they indicate the continuity of guidance in the present and the future. “And he made it”: and Abraham, blessings of God upon him, made the word of divine oneness he spoke — namely his saying “Indeed I am disassociated from what you worship except for He who created me” — “a word remaining among his descendants,” in his offspring, so there will always be among them one who affirms God’s oneness and calls to His oneness, so that perhaps those among them who associated others [with God] return through the call of those who affirmed oneness. Like it is “And Abraham instructed his sons with it.” It is also said: “and God made it.” It is also read “kalima” in the lightened form, and “fī ʿaqabihi” likewise, and “fī ʿāqibihi,” i.e., among those who came after him, i.e., his successors.
قلت: قال مرة فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ ومرّة فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ فاجمع بينهما وقدّر، كأنه قال. فهو يهدين وسيهدين، فيدلان على استمرار الهداية في الحال والاستقبال وَجَعَلَها وجعل إبراهيم صلوات الله عليه كلمة التوحيد التي تكلم بها وهي قوله إِنَّنِي بَراءٌ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي كَلِمَةً باقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ في ذريته، فلا يزال فيهم من يوحد الله ويدعو إلى توحيده، لعل من أشرك منهم يرجع بدعاء من وحد منهم. ونحوه وَوَصَّى بِها إِبْراهِيمُ بَنِيهِ وقيل: وجعلها الله. وقرئ: كلمة على التخفيف وفي عقبه كذلك، وفي عاقبه، أى: فيمن عقبه، أى: خلفه.

Q 43:29 · Vol. 4, pp. 246–247

Verse 29

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until the truth came to them and a clear messenger (29)
بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هؤُلاءِ وَآباءَهُمْ حَتَّى جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ (29)
Vol. 4, p. 246
“Rather, I gave enjoyment to these” — he means the people of Mecca, who are of the descendants of Abraham — by prolonging life and favour, so they were deluded by the respite and were preoccupied with luxury, following desires and obeying Satan, away from the word of oneness, “until the truth came to them,” which is the Qur’an, “and a clear messenger,” whose message is plain by the clear signs he has with him; so they denied him and called him a sorcerer and what he brought sorcery, and what Abraham hoped for did not occur from them. It is also read “matta ʿnā.”
بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هؤُلاءِ يعنى: أهل مكة، وهم من عقب إبراهيم بالمدّ في العمر والنعمة، فاغتروا بالمهلة، وشغلوا بالتنعم واتباع الشهوات وطاعة الشيطان عن كلمة التوحيد حَتَّى جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ وهو القرآن وَرَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ الرسالة واضحها بما معه من الآيات البينة، فكذبوا به وسموه ساحرا وما جاء به سحرا ولم يوجد منهم ما رجاه إبراهيم. وقرئ: بل متعنا.
Question
If you say: what is the aspect of the reading of one who read “mattaʿtu” with fatḥa on the tāʾ?
فإن قلت: فما وجه قراءة من قرأ مَتَّعْتُ بفتح التاء؟
Answer
I say: as if God Most High objected against Himself in His saying “and he made it a word remaining among his descendants, that perhaps they would return,"
قلت: كأن الله تعالى اعترض على ذاته في قوله وَجَعَلَها كَلِمَةً باقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
Vol. 4, p. 247
so He said: Rather, I gave them enjoyment with what I gave them enjoyment — long life and ampleness of provision — until that preoccupied them from the word of oneness. By that He intended elaboration in reproaching them, for if He gave them enjoyment by increase of favours, it was incumbent upon them to make that a cause of increased gratitude and steadfastness upon oneness and belief, not to associate others with Him and make rivals for Him. An example is that a man complains of the ill-treatment of one to whom he has been kind, then turns to himself and says: “You are the cause of that, by your kindness and favour,” his aim by this speech being to rebuke the wrongdoer, not to condemn his act.
فقال: بل متعتهم بما متعتهم به من طول العمر والسعة في الرزق، حتى شغلهم ذلك عن كلمة التوحيد. وأراد بذلك الإطناب في تعييرهم، لأنه إذا متعهم بزيادة النعم وجب عليهم أن يجعلوا ذلك سببا في زيادة الشكر والثبات على التوحيد والإيمان، لا أن يشركوا به ويجعلوا له أندادا، فمثاله أن يشكو الرجل إساءة من أحسن إليه، ثم يقبل على نفسه فيقول. أنت السبب في ذلك بمعروفك وإحسانك، وغرضه بهذا الكلام توبيخ المسيء لا تقبيح فعله.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 246
1. (1) . His saying “naḥwa karīm wa-karām”: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-karām — with ḍamma — is like al-karīm. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «نحو كريم وكرام» في الصحاح. الكرام- بالضم-: مثل الكريم. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 247
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “If you say: He made the coming of the truth and the messenger the limit of the enjoyment, then followed it … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: Precious words, to which nothing can be added — except that his saying “by this limit He suggested that they awakened at it” is a looseness to be avoided; and God knows best. And how fine is the coming of the limit in this manner, like the coming of “bal” (iḍrāb, ‘rather’) at some times: as the limit has come here — and what is meant by it is not that the act mentioned before it ceases at it, as is understood from it, but rather its continuation and increase, as though that beneficial state ended with the existence of what is more complete than it — so also the iḍrāb in such as His saying Most High “Rather, their knowledge concerning the Hereafter has been exhausted; rather, they are in doubt about it; rather, they are blind to it.” And these iḍrābs are not in the sense that the second of them is a rejection of the first; rather the second is more emphatic than the first, and the iḍrāb came with agreement and increase to indicate that the second, since it exceeds the first, becomes, by its excess and the first’s deficiency, as though they were two mutually exclusive things, the first being turned away from and the last affirmed; and the like is much; and in God is success.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «فان قلت: قد جعل مجيء الحق والرسول غاية التمتيع، ثم أردفه
…. الخ» قال أحمد: كلام نفيس لا مزيد عليه، إلا أن قوله: «خيل بهذه الغاية أنهم تنبهوا عندها» إطلاق ينبغي اجتنابه، والله أعلم وما أحسن مجيء الغاية على هذا النحو مجيء الاضراب في بعض التارات، فكما جاءت الغاية هنا- وليس المراد بها أن الفعل المذكور قبلها منقطع عندها على ما هو المفهوم منها، بل المراد استمراره وزيادته، فكأن تلك الحالة النافعة انتهت بوجود ما هو أكمل منها- كذلك الاضراب في مثل قوله تعالى بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْها بَلْ هُمْ مِنْها عَمُونَ وهذه الاضرابات ليست على معنى أن الثاني منها رد للأول، بل ثانيها آكد من أولها، وجاء الاضراب مع التوافق والزيادة للاشعار بأن الثاني لما زاد على الأول صار باعتبار زيادته ونقصان الأول كأنهما شيئان متنافيان يضرب عن أولهما ويثبت آخرهما، ومثله كثير وبالله التوفيق.

Q 43:30–31 · Vol. 4, pp. 247–248

Verses 30 to 31

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And when the truth came to them, they said, “This is magic, and indeed we are disbelievers in it” (30) And they said, “Why was this Qur’an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?” (31)
وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِ كافِرُونَ (30) وَقالُوا لَوْلا نُزِّلَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ (31)
Vol. 4, p. 247
Question
If you say: He made the coming of the truth and of the messenger the limit of the enjoyment, then followed it(1) with “And when the truth came to them they said: This is magic”; so what is the way of this composition and its import?
فإن قلت: قد جعل مجيء الحق والرسول غاية التمتيع، ثم أردفه «1» قوله وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ فما طريقة هذا النظم ومؤداه؟
Answer
I say: what is meant by “enjoyment” is what is a cause for it, namely their preoccupation with enjoyment away from oneness and what it requires; so He said: rather, they were preoccupied from oneness until the truth and a clear messenger came to them; so by this limit He suggested that they awakened at it from their heedlessness, since it calls for awakening; then He began their story at the coming of the truth, saying: when the truth came to them, they came with what is worse than their heedlessness in which they were: they added to their polytheism opposition to the truth, defiance of the Messenger and hostility to him, contempt for God’s Book and His laws, persistence in the acts of the disbelievers, and dictating to God’s wisdom in His choosing Muḥammad from among the people of his time, by their saying “Why was this Qur’an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?” — and that is the extreme in disfiguring the picture of their affair. It is read “ʿalā rajulin” with sukūn on the jīm; “from the two towns”: from one of the two towns, as in His saying Most High “From both of them come pearl and coral,” i.e., from one of them. The two towns are Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. It is also said: from the two men of the two towns, namely al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī and Ḥabīb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr al-Thaqafī, from Ibn ʿAbbās. And from Mujāhid: ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa and Kināna ibn ʿAbd Yālīl. And from Qatāda: al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd
قلت: المراد بالتمتيع ما هو سبب له، وهو اشتغالهم بالاستمتاع عن التوحيد ومقتضياته، فقال: بل اشتغلوا عن التوحيد حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين، فخيل بهذه الغاية أنهم تنبهوا عندها عن غفلتهم لاقتضائها التنبه، ثم ابتدأ قصتهم عند مجيء الحق فقال: ولما جاءهم الحق جاءوا بما هو شر من غفلتهم التي كانوا عليها: وهو أن ضموا إلى شركهم معاندة الحق، ومكابرة الرسول، ومعاداته، والاستخفاف بكتاب الله وشرائعه، والإصرار على أفعال الكفرة والاحتكام على حكمة الله في تخير محمد من أهل زمانه بقولهم لَوْلا نُزِّلَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ وهي الغاية في تشويه صورة أمرهم. قرئ على رجل، بسكون الجيم من القريتين: من إحدى القريتين، كقوله تعالى يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ أى من أحدهما. والقريتان: مكة والطائف. وقيل: من رجلي القريتين، وهما: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي وحبيب بن عمرو بن عمير الثقفي، عن ابن عباس. وعن مجاهد: عتبة بن ربيعة وكنانة بن عبد ياليل. وعن قتادة: الوليد بن المغيرة وعروة بن مسعود
Vol. 4, p. 248
al-Thaqafī; and al-Walīd used to say: “If what Muḥammad says were true, this Qur’an would have been sent down upon me or upon Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī” — and Abū Masʿūd is the kunya of ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd. They kept denying that God would send a human as a messenger; then when they learned, through God’s repetition of the arguments, that the messengers were only men from the people of the towns, they came with denial from another angle, namely their dictating that it be one of these two; and their saying “this Qur’an” was mentioned by way of belittling it; and by the man’s “greatness” they meant his leadership and precedence in this world; and it escaped their minds that the great one is he who is great with God.
الثقفي، وكان الوليد يقول: لو كان حقا ما يقول محمد لنزل هذا القرآن علىّ أو على أبى مسعود الثقفي، وأبو مسعود: كنية عروة بن مسعود ما زالوا ينكرون أن يبعث الله بشرا رسولا، فلما علموا بتكرير الله الحجج أن الرسل لم يكونوا إلا رجالا من أهل القرى، جاءوا بالإنكار من وجه آخر، وهو تحكمهم أن يكون أحد هذين، وقولهم: هذا القرآن ذكر له على وجه الاستهانة به، وأرادوا بعظم الرجل: رياسته وتقدّمه في الدنيا، وعزب عن عقولهم أن العظيم من كان عند الله عظيما.

Q 43:32 · Vol. 4, pp. 248–249

Verse 32

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate (32)
أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنا بَيْنَهُمْ مَعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَرَفَعْنا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ لِيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً سُخْرِيًّا وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ (32)
Vol. 4, p. 248
“Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?” This hamza is a self-sufficient denial, charging ignorance and expressing wonder at their objecting and dictating, and at their being the ones who manage the affair of prophethood and choose for it whoever is fit for it and will carry it out, and the ones who undertake the distribution of God’s mercy, which none undertakes but He by His dazzling power and consummate wisdom. Then He struck an example for them: He informed that they are incapable of managing even the most particular of their own affairs and what is good for them in their worldly life, and that God, Mighty and Exalted, is the One who distributed their livelihood among them, decreed it, and managed their conditions as one who knows them; so He did not make them equal, but made them differ in the means of livelihood and varied their ranks — making some strong and some weak, some rich and some needy, some masters and some servants — so that some of them put others to work in their needs, employ them in their trades and take them into service in their tasks, so that they live together, help one another, reach their benefits and obtain their conveniences; and had He left them to themselves and entrusted them with the management of their affair, they would have been lost and perished. And if they are in the management of base livelihood in worldly life in this condition, what do you think of them in managing the affairs of religion, which is God’s greatest mercy and supreme compassion, the road to securing the portions of the Hereafter and the ladder to arriving at the Abode of Peace? Then He said “and the mercy of your Lord,” meaning: and this mercy, which is God’s religion and the success in the final return that follows it, is better than what these accumulate of the debris of the world. If you say: their livelihood (maʿīsha) is that by which they live of benefits,(1) and some live by the lawful and some by the unlawful; so God Most High has thus distributed the unlawful as He distributed the lawful. I say: God Most High allotted to every servant his livelihood — his foods and drinks and what is good for him of benefits — and permitted him to take them, but made it a condition for him
أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ هذه الهمزة للإنكار المستقل بالتجهيل والتعجيب من اعتراضهم وتحكمهم، وأن يكونوا هم المدبرين لأمر النبوّة والتخير لها من يصلح لها ويقوم بها، والمتولين لقسمة رحمة الله التي لا يتولاها إلا هو بباهر قدرته وبالغ حكمته، ثم ضرب لهم مثلا فأعلم أنهم عاجزون عن تدبير خويصة أمرهم وما يصلحهم في دنياهم، وأنّ الله عزّ وعلا هو الذي قسم بينهم معيشتهم وقدرها ودبر أحوالهم تدبير العالم بها، فلم يسوّ بينهم ولكن فاوت بينهم في أسباب العيش، وغاير بين منازلهم فجعل منهم أقوياء وضعفاء وأغنياء ومحاويج وموالي وخدما، ليصرف بعضهم بعضا في حوائجهم ويستخدموهم في مهنهم ويتسخروهم في أشغالهم، حتى يتعايشوا ويترافدوا ويصلوا إلى منافعهم ويحصلوا على مرافقهم، ولو وكلهم إلى أنفسهم وولاهم تدبير أمرهم، لضاعوا وهلكوا. وإذا كانوا في تدبير المعيشة الدنية في الحياة الدنيا على هذه الصفة، فما ظنك بهم في تدبير أمور الدين الذي هو رحمة الله الكبرى ورأفته العظمى؟ وهو الطريق إلى حيازة حظوظ الآخرة والسلم إلى حلول دار السلام؟ ثم قال وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ يريد: وهذه الرحمة وهي دين الله وما يتبعه من الفوز في المآب: خير مما يجمع هؤلاء من حطام الدنيا. فان قلت: معيشتهم ما يعيشون به من المنافع «1» ، ومنهم من يعيش بالحلال، ومنهم من يعيش بالحرام، فإذن قد قسم الله تعالى الحرام كما قسم الحلال. قلت: الله تعالى قسم لكل عبد معيشته وهي مطاعمه ومشاربه وما يصلحه من المنافع وأذن له في تناولها، ولكن شرط عليه
Vol. 4, p. 249
and charged him to follow, in taking them, the way He legislated; so if he follows it, he has taken his allotted portion of livelihood lawfully and called it God’s provision; and if he does not follow it, he takes it unlawfully, and he may not call it God’s provision;(1) so God Most High is the distributor of livelihoods and benefits, but it is the servants who give them the attribute of being unlawful by their evil taking of them, namely their deviating in it from what God legislated to what He did not legislate.
وكلفه أن يسلك في تناولها الطريق التي شرعها، فإذا سلكها فقد تناول قسمته من المعيشة حلالا، وسماها رزق الله، وإذا لم يسلكها تناولها حراما، وليس له أن يسميها رزق الله «1» ، فالله تعالى قاسم المعايش والمنافع، ولكن العباد هم الذين يكسبونها صفة الحرمة بسوء تناولهم، وهو عدولهم فيه عما شرعه الله إلى ما لم يشرعه.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 248
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “If you say: their livelihood is that by which they live of benefits … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: It has preceded that provision (rizq), according to the people of the Sunna, is applied to what God sustains the servant’s condition with, whether lawful or unlawful; and this verse supports it; and al-Zamakhsharī built on his [Muʿtazilī] principle, and that has preceded.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «فان قلت: معيشتهم ما يعيشون به من المنافع
…. الخ» قال أحمد: قد تقدم أن الرزق عند أهل السنة يطلق على ما يقوم الله به حال العبد حلالا كان أو حراما، وهذه الآية معضدة، والزمخشري بنى على أصله وقد تقدم.
Vol. 4, p. 249
1. (1) . His saying “wa-laysa lahu an yusammiyahā rizq Allāh”: this is on the school of the Muʿtazila. As for the people of the Sunna, provision is what is benefited from, even if unlawful. The author means that God does not facilitate the unlawful, because He does not do the ugly according to the Muʿtazila. The school of the people of the Sunna is that the doer of all that exists is God Most High. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Its meaning: were it not for the aversion that they unite upon disbelief, We would have made for the disbelievers roofs of silver, i.e., We would have given them ample [share of] this world because of its insignificance with Us.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: “Lawlā” here is the sister of “lawlā” in His saying “And if only [it were not that] a calamity would strike them for what their hands have put forth” — the verse. There, the speech is made sound by estimating the aversion to that, by not estimating something omitted as I presented earlier; so the aspect of the speech here is that their unanimity upon disbelief is a preventer of the spreading out of this world. And this is the meaning of “lawlā” in general: that what follows it is always a preventer of its answer; but at times the preventer is actually existent, so the answer is impossible without difficulty, as in His saying Most High “Were it not for God’s favour upon you and His mercy, you would have been among the losers,” and this is most common. And at times its existence is by estimation along with it, and on that is the verse, i.e., were the spreading out of the world for the disbeliever to exist by estimation, its preventer would be found with Us, namely unanimity upon disbelief, by estimation along with it; and everything whose existence leads to the existence of its preventer is not found.
1. (1) . قوله «وليس له أن يسميها رزق الله» هذا على مذهب المعتزلة. وأما عند أهل السنة فالرزق ما ينتفع به ولو حراما. والمصنف يريد أن الله لا ييسر الحرام، لأنه لا يفعل القبيح عند المعتزلة. ومذهب أهل السنة أن فاعل الكائنات كلها هو الله تعالى. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «معناه لولا كراهية أن يجتمعوا على الكفر لجعلنا للكفرة سقوفا من فضة أى لوسعنا عليهم الدنيا لحقارتها عندنا» قال أحمد: «لولا» هنا أخت «لولا» في قوله وَلَوْلا أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ
…. الآية تلك أن تصحح الكلام بتقدير كراهة ذلك بأن لا تقدر محذوفا كما قدمته، فيكون وجه الكلام هاهنا أن إجماعهم على الكفر مانع من بسط الدنيا. وهذا هو معنى لولا المطرد أن ما بعدها أبدا مانع من جوابها، ولكن قد يكون المانع موجودا تحقيقا فيمتنع الجواب بلا إشكال، كقوله تعالى فَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنْتُمْ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ وهو الأكثر. وقد يكون وجوده تقديرا معه وعلى ذلك الآية، أى: لو وجد بسط الدنيا للكافر مقدرا، لوجد مانعه عندنا وهو الاجتماع على الكفر مقدرا معه، وكل ما أدى وجوده إلى وجود مانعه لا يوجد.

Verses 33 to 35

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And were it not that mankind would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses, roofs of silver and stairways upon which to mount (33) and for their houses, doors and couches upon which to recline (34) and gold ornament. And all that is nothing but the enjoyment of worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous (35)
وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَمَعارِجَ عَلَيْها يَظْهَرُونَ (33) وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْواباً وَسُرُراً عَلَيْها يَتَّكِؤُنَ (34) وَزُخْرُفاً وَإِنْ كُلُّ ذلِكَ لَمَّا مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (35)
Vol. 4, p. 249
“For their houses” is a substitute of inclusion for His saying “for those who disbelieve”; and it is possible that the two lāms be like the two lāms in your saying “I gave him a garment for his shirt.” It is also read “suqufan” with fatḥa on the sīn and sukūn on the qāf; and with ḍamma on it and sukūn on the qāf, and with ḍamma on both: plural of “saqf,” like “rahn,” “ruhn” and “ruhun.” From al-Farrāʾ: plural of “saqīfa”; and “saqafan” with two fatḥas, as though it were a dialect form of “saqf”; and “suqūfan”; “maʿārij” and “maʿārīj.” Al-maʿārij: plural of “maʿraj,” or a collective noun for “miʿrāj”: which are the ascents to the upper chambers. “Upon which to mount”: i.e., upon the stairways, they mount to the roofs, climbing them; “and they could not scale it.” “Sururan”: with fatḥa on the rāʾ, because of the heaviness of two ḍammas with two doubled letters. “Lammā matāʿ al-ḥayāt”: the lām is the one that distinguishes the lightened “inna” from the negative. It is also read with kasra on the lām, i.e., “that which is the enjoyment of life,” like His saying Most High “as an example, what is a gnat”; and “lammā” with intensification, in the sense of “illā,” with “in” as a negative. It is also read “illā.” And it is read “wa-mā kullu dhālika illā.” When He said “better than what they accumulate,” and thereby belittled and diminished the matter of this world, He followed it with what establishes the paltriness of this world with Him: His saying “And were it not that mankind would become one community,” i.e., were it not for the aversion that they unite upon disbelief and be wholly engaged in it, We would have made — because of the insignificance of the bloom of the worldly life(2) with Us — for the disbelievers roofs, ascents, doors and couches, all of them
لِبُيُوتِهِمْ بدل اشتمال من قوله لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ ويجوز أن يكونا بمنزلة اللامين في قولك: وهبت له ثوبا لقميصه. وقرئ: سقفا، بفتح السين وسكون القاف. وبضمها وسكون القاف وبضمها: جمع سقف، كرهن ورهن ورهن. وعن الفراء: جمع سقيفة وسقفا بفتحتين، كأنه لغة في سقف وسقوفا، ومعارج ومعاريج. والمعارج: جمع معرج، أو اسم جمع لمعراج: وهي المصاعد إلى العلالي عَلَيْها يَظْهَرُونَ أى على المعارج، يظهرون السطوح يعلونها، فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه. وسررا، بفتح الراء لاستثقال الضمتين مع حرفى التضعيف لَمَّا مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ اللام هي الفارقة بين إن المخففة والنافية. وقرئ بكسر اللام، أى: الذي هو متاع الحياة، كقوله تعالى مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةً ولما بالتشديد بمعنى إلا، وإن نافية. وقرئ: إلا. وقرئ: وما كل ذلك إلا. لما قال خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ فقلل أمر الدنيا وصغرها: أردفه ما يقرّر قلة الدنيا عنده من قوله وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً أى: ولولا كراهة أن يجتمعوا على الكفر ويطبقوا عليه، لجعلنا لحقارة زهرة الحياة الدنيا «2» عندنا للكفار سقوفا ومصاعد وأبوابا وسررا كلها
Vol. 4, p. 250
of silver and gold ornament; and We would have given them ornament (zukhruf), i.e., adornment of everything. Al-zukhruf: adornment and gold. It is also possible that the original is “suqufan min fiḍḍa wa-zukhruf,” meaning: some of it of silver and some of gold; so it is accusative as a conjunction upon the position of “min fiḍḍa.” In its sense is the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ: “If this world weighed with God the wing of a gnat, He would not give a disbeliever a drink of water from it.”(1)
من فضة وزخرف، وجعلنا لهم زخرفا، أى: زينة من كل شيء. والزخرف: الزينة والذهب. ويجوز أن يكون الأصل: سقفا من فضة وزخرف، يعنى: بعضها من فضة وبعضها من ذهب، فنصب عطفا على محل مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وفي معناه قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لو وزنت الدنيا عند الله جناح بعوضة ما سقى الكافر منها شربة ماء» «1»
Question
If you say: since He did not give the disbelievers ample [share] because of the trial to which giving them ampleness would lead — namely people’s total engagement in disbelief out of love of this world and their rushing upon it — why did He not give the Muslims ampleness so that people be wholly engaged in Islam?
فإن قلت: فحين لم يوسع على الكافرين للفتنة التي كان يؤدّى إليها التوسعة عليهم من إطباق الناس على الكفر لحبهم الدنيا وتهالكهم عليها، فهلا وسع على المسلمين ليطبق الناس على الإسلام؟
Answer
I say: giving them ampleness is also a corruption, because of what it leads to of entering Islam for the sake of this world, and entering the religion for the sake of this world is the religion of the hypocrites;(2) so the wisdom was in what He arranged, in that He made in both parties rich and poor, and made poverty prevail over wealth.
قلت: التوسعة عليهم مفسدة أيضا لما تؤدى إليه من الدخول في الإسلام لأجل الدنيا، والدخول في الدين لأجل الدنيا من دين المنافقين «2» ، فكانت الحكمة فيما دبر: حيث جعل في الفريقين أغنياء وفقراء، وغلب الفقر على الغنى.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 249
1. (1) . His saying “wa-laysa lahu an yusammiyahā rizq Allāh”: this is on the school of the Muʿtazila. As for the people of the Sunna, provision is what is benefited from, even if unlawful. The author means that God does not facilitate the unlawful, because He does not do the ugly according to the Muʿtazila. The school of the people of the Sunna is that the doer of all that exists is God Most High. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Its meaning: were it not for the aversion that they unite upon disbelief, We would have made for the disbelievers roofs of silver, i.e., We would have given them ample [share of] this world because of its insignificance with Us.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: “Lawlā” here is the sister of “lawlā” in His saying “And if only [it were not that] a calamity would strike them for what their hands have put forth” — the verse. There, the speech is made sound by estimating the aversion to that, by not estimating something omitted as I presented earlier; so the aspect of the speech here is that their unanimity upon disbelief is a preventer of the spreading out of this world. And this is the meaning of “lawlā” in general: that what follows it is always a preventer of its answer; but at times the preventer is actually existent, so the answer is impossible without difficulty, as in His saying Most High “Were it not for God’s favour upon you and His mercy, you would have been among the losers,” and this is most common. And at times its existence is by estimation along with it, and on that is the verse, i.e., were the spreading out of the world for the disbeliever to exist by estimation, its preventer would be found with Us, namely unanimity upon disbelief, by estimation along with it; and everything whose existence leads to the existence of its preventer is not found.
1. (1) . قوله «وليس له أن يسميها رزق الله» هذا على مذهب المعتزلة. وأما عند أهل السنة فالرزق ما ينتفع به ولو حراما. والمصنف يريد أن الله لا ييسر الحرام، لأنه لا يفعل القبيح عند المعتزلة. ومذهب أهل السنة أن فاعل الكائنات كلها هو الله تعالى. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «معناه لولا كراهية أن يجتمعوا على الكفر لجعلنا للكفرة سقوفا من فضة أى لوسعنا عليهم الدنيا لحقارتها عندنا» قال أحمد: «لولا» هنا أخت «لولا» في قوله وَلَوْلا أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ
…. الآية تلك أن تصحح الكلام بتقدير كراهة ذلك بأن لا تقدر محذوفا كما قدمته، فيكون وجه الكلام هاهنا أن إجماعهم على الكفر مانع من بسط الدنيا. وهذا هو معنى لولا المطرد أن ما بعدها أبدا مانع من جوابها، ولكن قد يكون المانع موجودا تحقيقا فيمتنع الجواب بلا إشكال، كقوله تعالى فَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنْتُمْ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ وهو الأكثر. وقد يكون وجوده تقديرا معه وعلى ذلك الآية، أى: لو وجد بسط الدنيا للكافر مقدرا، لوجد مانعه عندنا وهو الاجتماع على الكفر مقدرا معه، وكل ما أدى وجوده إلى وجود مانعه لا يوجد.
Vol. 4, p. 250
1. (1) . In it is ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Sulaymān, and Zakariyyā ibn Manẓūr followed him. Al-Tirmidhī said: And on this topic there is a report from Abū Hurayra, whose ḥadīth is in al-Bazzār from the ḥadīth of Ṣāliḥ, freedman of al-Tawʾama, from him; and its wording: “Not a thing of it would be given to a disbeliever.” Al-Bayhaqī narrated it in al-Shuʿab, in the seventy-first [section], from the narration of Abū Maʿshar, from al-Maqburī, from him. And on this topic there is a report from Ibn ʿAbbās recorded by Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilya, in which is al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmāra, who is very weak. And al-Quḍāʿī recorded it in Musnad al-Shihāb from the narration of Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, with the author’s wording. Ibn Ṭāhir said: In it is ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAwf, from Abū Muṣʿab, from him; it has no basis from the ḥadīth of Mālik.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Since He did not give the disbelievers ample [share] because of the trial to which ampleness led — total engagement in disbelief — why did He not give the Muslims ampleness so that people be wholly engaged in belief? And he answered that giving them ampleness is also a corruption because of what it leads to of entering Islam for the sake of this world, and that is of the religion of the hypocrites.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: A question and an answer built on two invalid principles. One: giving causes (taʿlīl) for God Most High’s acts; the other: that God Most High willed Islam from all of creation. As for the first, God silenced the questioner about it with His saying “He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned”; and as for the second, God spared the believers the answer to it with His saying “And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together.”
3. . Maḥmūd said: “One says ʿashiya baṣaruhu — with kasra on the shīn — when affliction befalls it … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: In this verse there are two ingenious points. One: the indication that an indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition gives generality — a question in which the legal theorists (uṣūliyyūn) were unsettled; and the Imām al-Ḥaramayn is among those who say that it gives generality, to the point that he corrected the imams for their unqualified statement that an indefinite noun in the context of affirmation is particular, and said: the condition is general, and an indefinite noun in its context is general. The jurist Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī al-Anbārī, the commentator on his book, refuted him harshly. And in this verse there is sufficiency for the Imām and for those who say as he does, because the devil is mentioned in it as indefinite in the context of a condition, and we know that what is meant is the generality of devils, not one, for two reasons: one, that it is established that every person has a devil, so how of one who turns away from the remembrance of God; the other, drawn from the verse: that He returned the pronoun to it in the plural in His saying “and indeed they,” which returns to the devil, by a single account; and were it not for its giving generality of inclusion, the return of a plural pronoun to it would not be permissible, without difficulty. So this is a point at whose hearing you find the opponents of this view silenced. The second point: that in this verse is a refutation of those who claim that returning [the pronoun] by the sense of “man” prevents returning by its wording afterwards. The one who prevents this argued that it is generality after specification, which is contrary to the known standard of eloquence. Al-Kindī refuted this with His saying Most High “And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever; God has made good for him provision,” and another refuted it with His saying “And among the people is he who buys idle talk to mislead from the path of God without knowledge and takes it in ridicule — those will have a humiliating punishment. And when Our verses are recited to him …” — the verse. And my grandfather ؒ had drawn out some of this from this verse, because he returned to the wording in His saying “yaʿshu” and “lahu” twice, then to the sense in His saying “la-yaṣuddūnahum,” then to the wording in His saying “ḥattā idhā jāʾanā.” And I mentioned earlier that the one who prevented that may have limited his prevention to its coming in a single sentence, but when sentences are multiple and each stands by itself, that may not be prevented — until I rebutted al-Zamakhsharī on His saying Most High “They will not possess intercession except he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful,” for there the sentence is one; so look at it in its place.
1. (1) . فيه عبد الحميد بن سليمان وتابعه زكريا بن منظور. وقال الترمذي: وفي الباب عن أبى هريرة، وحديثه عند البزار من حديث صالح مولى التوأمة عنه. ولفظه «ما أعطي كافرا منها شيئا» ورواه البيهقي في الشعب في الحادي والسبعين من رواية أبى معشر عن المقبري عنه وفي الباب عن ابن عباس. أخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية. وفيه الحسن ابن عمارة وهو ضعيف جدا. وأخرجه القضاعي في مسند الشهاب من رواية مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر، بلفظ المصنف قال ابن طاهر: فيه على بن محمد بن أحمد بن أبى عوف عن أبى مصعب عنه، لا أصل له من حديث ملك
2. . قال محمود: «فحين لم يوسع على الكافرين للفتنة التي كان يؤدى إليها التوسعة من الاطباق على الكفر» فهلا وسع على المسلمين ليطبق الناس على الايمان؟ وأجاب بأن التوسعة عليهم مفسدة أيضا لما يؤدى إليه من الدخول في الإسلام لأجل الدنيا، وذلك من دين المنافقين» قال أحمد: سؤال وجواب مبنيان على قاعدتين فاسدتين. إحداهما: تعليل أفعال الله تعالى، والأخرى: أن الله تعالى أراد الإسلام من الخلق أجمعين. أما الأولى فقد أخرس الله السائل عنه بقوله لا يُسْئَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْئَلُونَ وأما الثانية فقد كفى الله المؤمنين الجواب عنه فيه بقوله وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً.
3. . قال محمود: «يقال عشى بصره بكسر الشين إذا أصابته الآفة
…. » قال أحمد: في هذه الآية نكتتان بديعتان، إحداهما: الدلالة على أن النكرة الواقعة في سياق الشرط تفيد العموم، وهي مسألة اضطرب فيها الأصوليون وإمام الحرمين من القائلين بافادتها العموم، حتى استدرك على الأئمة إطلاقهم القول بأن النكرة في سياق الإثبات تخص، وقال: إن الشرط يعم، والنكرة في سياقه تعم. وقد رد عليه الفقيه أبو الحسن على الأنبارى شارح كتابه ردا عنيفا. وفي هذه الآية للإمام ومن قال بقوله كفاية، وذلك أن الشيطان ذكر فيها منكرا في سياق شرط، ونحن نعلم أنه إنما أراد عموم الشياطين لا واحدا لوجهين، أحدهما: أنه قد ثبت أن لكل أحد شيطانا، فكيف بالعاشى عن ذكر الله، والآخر: يؤخذ من الآية: وهو أنه أعاد عليه الضمير مجموعا في قوله وَإِنَّهُمْ فانه عائد إلى الشيطان قولا واحدا «ولولا إفادته عموم الشمول لما جاز عود ضمير الجمع عليه بلا إشكال، فهذه نكتة تجد عند إسماعها لمخالفي هذا الرأى سكتة. والنكتة الثانية: أن في هذه الآية ردا على من زعم أن العود على معنى من يمنع من العود على لفظها بعد ذلك. واحتج المانع لذلك بأنه إجمال بعد تفسير، وهو خلاف المعهود من الفصاحة. وقد نقض الكندي هذا بقوله تعالى وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقاً ونقض غيره بقوله وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّخِذَها هُزُواً أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ
…. الآية وكان جدي رحمه الله قد استخرج من هذه الآية بعض ذلك، لأنه أعاد على اللفظ في قوله: يَعْشُ ولَهُ مرتين، ثم على المعنى في قوله لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ ثم على اللفظ بقوله حَتَّى إِذا جاءَنا وقد قدمت أن الذي منع ذلك قد يكون اقتصر بمنعه على مجيء ذلك في جملة واحدة وأما إذا تعددت الجمل واستفلت كل بنفسها فقد لا يمنع ذلك حتى رددت على الزمخشري في قوله تعالى لا يَمْلِكُونَ الشَّفاعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمنِ عَهْداً فان الجملة واحدة، فانظره في موضعه.

Q 43:36–39 · Vol. 4, pp. 250–253

Verses 36 to 39

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And whoever turns away (yaʿshu) from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion (36) And indeed, they [the devils] avert them from the path while they think that they are guided (37) Until, when he comes to Us, he says, “Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts — what an evil companion!” (38) And never will it benefit you today, when you have wronged, that you are sharers in the punishment (39)
وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ (36) وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ (37) حَتَّى إِذا جاءَنا قالَ يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ (38) وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ (39)
Vol. 4, p. 250
It is read “yaʿshu” with ḍamma on the shīn and with fatḥa. The difference between them is that when the affliction occurs in his sight it is said “ʿashiya”; and when he looks with the look of the night-blind though there is no affliction in him, it is said “ʿashā.” A parallel is “ʿarija” for one who has the affliction,(3)
قرئ: ومن يعش، بضم الشين وفتحها. والفرق بينهما أنه إذا حصلت الآفة في بصره قيل: عشى. وإذا نظر نظر العشى ولا آفة به قيل عشا. ونظيره: عرج، لمن به الآفة «3» .
Vol. 4, p. 251
and “ʿaraja” for one who walks the walk of the lame without lameness. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said: “Whenever you come to him, you gaze dimly toward the light of his fire.”(1) That is: you look at it as the night-blind look, because your sight weakens from the greatness of the fuel and the breadth of the light. It is clear in Ḥātim’s saying: “I look dimly aside whenever my neighbour-woman comes out, until her chamber-curtain covers my neighbour-woman.”(2)
وعرج، لمن مشى مشية العرجان من غير عرج. قال الحطيئة: متى تأته تعشو إلى ضوء ناره «1» أى: تنظر إليها نظر العشىّ لما يضعف بصرك من عظم الوقود واتساع الضوء. وهو بين في قوله حاتم: أعشو إذا ما جارتى برزت … حتّى يوارى جارتى الخدر «2»
Vol. 4, p. 252
It is also read “yaʿshū,” on the basis that “man” is relative [not conditional], not implying the sense of condition; and the one who reads so ought to put “nuqayyiḍ” in the nominative [“nuqayyiḍu”]. The meaning of the reading with fatḥa: “whoever is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful,” which is the Qur’an, as in His saying Most High “deaf, dumb, blind.” As for the reading with ḍamma, its meaning is: whoever feigns blindness to His remembrance, i.e., knows that it is the truth yet pretends ignorance and dullness, as in His saying Most High “And they rejected them, while their souls were convinced of them.” “We appoint for him a devil”: We forsake him(1) and leave him to the devils, as in His saying Most High “And We appointed for them companions,” “Do you not see that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers?” It is also read “yuqayyiḍ,” i.e., the Most Merciful appoints for him and the devil appoints for him.
وقرئ: يعشو، على أنّ من موصولة غير مضمنة معنى الشرط. وحق هذا القارئ أن يرفع نقيض. ومعنى القراءة بالفتح: ومن يعم عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمنِ وهو القرآن، كقوله تعالى صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ وأما القراءة بالضم فمعناها: ومن يتعام عن ذكره، أى: يعرف أنه الحق وهو يتجاهل ويتغابى، كقوله تعالى وَجَحَدُوا بِها وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْها أَنْفُسُهُمْ. نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطاناً نخذله «1» ونخل بينه وبين الشياطين، كقوله تعالى وَقَيَّضْنا لَهُمْ قُرَناءَ، أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ وقرئ: يقيض، أى: يقيض له الرحمن ويقيض له الشيطان.
Question
If you say: why was the pronoun of “man” and the pronoun of “the devil” made plural in His saying “and indeed they avert them”?
فإن قلت: لم جمع ضمير من وضمير الشيطان في قوله وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ؟
Answer
I say: because “man” is indeterminate as to the kind of the one turning away, and an indeterminate devil has been appointed for him as to kind; so when it was possible for them, by their indeterminacy, to include more than one, it was possible for the pronoun to return to them in the plural. “Until, when he comes to Us”: the one who turns away. It is also read “jāʾānā,” on the basis that the verb is for him and for his devil. “He says,” to his devil: “Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts,” meaning the east and the west, giving precedence [to one], as it is said “the two ʿUmars” and “the two moons.”
قلت: لأنّ مَنْ مبهم في جنس العاشى، وقد قيض له شيطان مبهم في جنسه، فلما جاز أن يتناولا لإبهامهما غير واحدين: جاز أن يرجع الضمير إليهما مجموعا حَتَّى إِذا جاءَنا العاشى. وقرئ: جاءانا، على أنّ الفعل له ولشيطانه. قالَ لشيطانه يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ يريد المشرق والمغرب، فغلب. كما قيل: العمران والقمران.
Question
If you say: what is “the distance of the two easts”?
فإن قلت: فما بعد المشرقين؟
Answer
I say: their remoteness from each other; the original is “the distance of the east from the west and the west from the east”; so when one made the weightier prevail and combined the two separate things in a dual, he annexed the distance to them. “Annakum” is in the position of the nominative as agent, meaning: it will never benefit you, your being sharers in the punishment, as sharing benefits those who are in a hard matter, through their helping one another in bearing its burdens and dividing its severity and hardship; for each one of you has of the punishment what his capacity does not reach. You may also make the verb refer to the wish in His saying “Oh, would that between me and you,” in the sense: never will benefit you today what you are in of wishing the distance of the companion; and His saying “that you are sharers in the punishment” is a reason, i.e., your wishing will not benefit you, because it is your due that you and your companions share in the punishment as you were sharers in its cause, which is disbelief. It is strengthened by the reading of one who read “innakum” with kasra. It is also said: when the afflicted one (al-mamnuw)(2) sees someone afflicted with the like of his hardship, that eases him and relieves some of his distress, and that is the consolation (taʾassī) which al-Khansāʾ mentioned:
قلت: تباعدهما، والأصل: بعد المشرق من المغرب، والمغرب من المشرق. فلما غلب وجمع المفترقين بالتثنية: أضاف البعد إليهما أَنَّكُمْ في محل الرفع على الفاعلية، يعنى: ولن ينفعكم كونكم مشتركين في العذاب كما ينفع الواقعين في الأمر الصعب اشتراكهم فيه، لتعاونهم في تحمل أعبائه وتقسمهم لشدّته وعنائه، وذلك أنّ كل واحد منكم به من العذاب ما لا تبلغه طاقته، ولك أن تجعل الفعل للتمني في قوله يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ على معنى: ولن ينفعكم اليوم ما أنتم فيه من تمنى مباعدة القرين. وقوله أَنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ تعليل، أى: لن ينفعكم تمنيكم، لأنّ حقكم أن تشتركوا أنتم وقرناؤكم في العذاب كما كنتم مشتركين في سببه وهو الكفر. وتقوّيه قراءة من قرأ: إنكم بالكسر. وقيل: إذا رأى الممنوّ بشدّة «2» من منى بمثلها: روّحه ذلك ونفس بعض كربه، وهو التأسى الذي ذكرته الخنساء:
Vol. 4, p. 253
“I console myself over him with consolation (taʾassī).”(1) So these are not consoled by their sharing, nor are they eased, because of the greatness of what they are in.
أعزى النّفس عنه بالتّأسى «1» فهؤلاء لا يؤسيهم اشتراكهم ولا يروّحهم، لعظم ما هم فيه.
Question
If you say: what is the meaning of His saying Most High “when you have wronged”?
فإن قلت: ما معنى قوله تعالى إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ؟
Answer
I say: its meaning: when your wrongdoing has been established and made clear and no doubt remains for you or anyone that you were wrongdoers, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. “Idh” is a substitute for “today.” A parallel is: “When we trace our lineage, no base woman bore me”(2) — i.e., it became clear that I am the son of a noble woman.
قلت: معناه: إذ صح ظلمكم وتبين ولم يبق لكم ولا لأحد شبهة في أنكم كنتم ظالمين، وذلك يوم القيامة. وإذ: بدل من اليوم. ونظيره: إذا ما انتسبنا لم تلدني لئيمة «2» أى: تبين أنى ولد كريمة.
Editor’s notes on these 4 pages
Vol. 4, p. 250
1. (1) . In it is ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Sulaymān, and Zakariyyā ibn Manẓūr followed him. Al-Tirmidhī said: And on this topic there is a report from Abū Hurayra, whose ḥadīth is in al-Bazzār from the ḥadīth of Ṣāliḥ, freedman of al-Tawʾama, from him; and its wording: “Not a thing of it would be given to a disbeliever.” Al-Bayhaqī narrated it in al-Shuʿab, in the seventy-first [section], from the narration of Abū Maʿshar, from al-Maqburī, from him. And on this topic there is a report from Ibn ʿAbbās recorded by Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilya, in which is al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmāra, who is very weak. And al-Quḍāʿī recorded it in Musnad al-Shihāb from the narration of Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, with the author’s wording. Ibn Ṭāhir said: In it is ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAwf, from Abū Muṣʿab, from him; it has no basis from the ḥadīth of Mālik.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Since He did not give the disbelievers ample [share] because of the trial to which ampleness led — total engagement in disbelief — why did He not give the Muslims ampleness so that people be wholly engaged in belief? And he answered that giving them ampleness is also a corruption because of what it leads to of entering Islam for the sake of this world, and that is of the religion of the hypocrites.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: A question and an answer built on two invalid principles. One: giving causes (taʿlīl) for God Most High’s acts; the other: that God Most High willed Islam from all of creation. As for the first, God silenced the questioner about it with His saying “He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned”; and as for the second, God spared the believers the answer to it with His saying “And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together.”
3. . Maḥmūd said: “One says ʿashiya baṣaruhu — with kasra on the shīn — when affliction befalls it … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: In this verse there are two ingenious points. One: the indication that an indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition gives generality — a question in which the legal theorists (uṣūliyyūn) were unsettled; and the Imām al-Ḥaramayn is among those who say that it gives generality, to the point that he corrected the imams for their unqualified statement that an indefinite noun in the context of affirmation is particular, and said: the condition is general, and an indefinite noun in its context is general. The jurist Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī al-Anbārī, the commentator on his book, refuted him harshly. And in this verse there is sufficiency for the Imām and for those who say as he does, because the devil is mentioned in it as indefinite in the context of a condition, and we know that what is meant is the generality of devils, not one, for two reasons: one, that it is established that every person has a devil, so how of one who turns away from the remembrance of God; the other, drawn from the verse: that He returned the pronoun to it in the plural in His saying “and indeed they,” which returns to the devil, by a single account; and were it not for its giving generality of inclusion, the return of a plural pronoun to it would not be permissible, without difficulty. So this is a point at whose hearing you find the opponents of this view silenced. The second point: that in this verse is a refutation of those who claim that returning [the pronoun] by the sense of “man” prevents returning by its wording afterwards. The one who prevents this argued that it is generality after specification, which is contrary to the known standard of eloquence. Al-Kindī refuted this with His saying Most High “And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever; God has made good for him provision,” and another refuted it with His saying “And among the people is he who buys idle talk to mislead from the path of God without knowledge and takes it in ridicule — those will have a humiliating punishment. And when Our verses are recited to him …” — the verse. And my grandfather ؒ had drawn out some of this from this verse, because he returned to the wording in His saying “yaʿshu” and “lahu” twice, then to the sense in His saying “la-yaṣuddūnahum,” then to the wording in His saying “ḥattā idhā jāʾanā.” And I mentioned earlier that the one who prevented that may have limited his prevention to its coming in a single sentence, but when sentences are multiple and each stands by itself, that may not be prevented — until I rebutted al-Zamakhsharī on His saying Most High “They will not possess intercession except he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful,” for there the sentence is one; so look at it in its place.
1. (1) . فيه عبد الحميد بن سليمان وتابعه زكريا بن منظور. وقال الترمذي: وفي الباب عن أبى هريرة، وحديثه عند البزار من حديث صالح مولى التوأمة عنه. ولفظه «ما أعطي كافرا منها شيئا» ورواه البيهقي في الشعب في الحادي والسبعين من رواية أبى معشر عن المقبري عنه وفي الباب عن ابن عباس. أخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية. وفيه الحسن ابن عمارة وهو ضعيف جدا. وأخرجه القضاعي في مسند الشهاب من رواية مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر، بلفظ المصنف قال ابن طاهر: فيه على بن محمد بن أحمد بن أبى عوف عن أبى مصعب عنه، لا أصل له من حديث ملك
2. . قال محمود: «فحين لم يوسع على الكافرين للفتنة التي كان يؤدى إليها التوسعة من الاطباق على الكفر» فهلا وسع على المسلمين ليطبق الناس على الايمان؟ وأجاب بأن التوسعة عليهم مفسدة أيضا لما يؤدى إليه من الدخول في الإسلام لأجل الدنيا، وذلك من دين المنافقين» قال أحمد: سؤال وجواب مبنيان على قاعدتين فاسدتين. إحداهما: تعليل أفعال الله تعالى، والأخرى: أن الله تعالى أراد الإسلام من الخلق أجمعين. أما الأولى فقد أخرس الله السائل عنه بقوله لا يُسْئَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْئَلُونَ وأما الثانية فقد كفى الله المؤمنين الجواب عنه فيه بقوله وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً.
3. . قال محمود: «يقال عشى بصره بكسر الشين إذا أصابته الآفة
…. » قال أحمد: في هذه الآية نكتتان بديعتان، إحداهما: الدلالة على أن النكرة الواقعة في سياق الشرط تفيد العموم، وهي مسألة اضطرب فيها الأصوليون وإمام الحرمين من القائلين بافادتها العموم، حتى استدرك على الأئمة إطلاقهم القول بأن النكرة في سياق الإثبات تخص، وقال: إن الشرط يعم، والنكرة في سياقه تعم. وقد رد عليه الفقيه أبو الحسن على الأنبارى شارح كتابه ردا عنيفا. وفي هذه الآية للإمام ومن قال بقوله كفاية، وذلك أن الشيطان ذكر فيها منكرا في سياق شرط، ونحن نعلم أنه إنما أراد عموم الشياطين لا واحدا لوجهين، أحدهما: أنه قد ثبت أن لكل أحد شيطانا، فكيف بالعاشى عن ذكر الله، والآخر: يؤخذ من الآية: وهو أنه أعاد عليه الضمير مجموعا في قوله وَإِنَّهُمْ فانه عائد إلى الشيطان قولا واحدا «ولولا إفادته عموم الشمول لما جاز عود ضمير الجمع عليه بلا إشكال، فهذه نكتة تجد عند إسماعها لمخالفي هذا الرأى سكتة. والنكتة الثانية: أن في هذه الآية ردا على من زعم أن العود على معنى من يمنع من العود على لفظها بعد ذلك. واحتج المانع لذلك بأنه إجمال بعد تفسير، وهو خلاف المعهود من الفصاحة. وقد نقض الكندي هذا بقوله تعالى وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقاً ونقض غيره بقوله وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّخِذَها هُزُواً أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ
…. الآية وكان جدي رحمه الله قد استخرج من هذه الآية بعض ذلك، لأنه أعاد على اللفظ في قوله: يَعْشُ ولَهُ مرتين، ثم على المعنى في قوله لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ ثم على اللفظ بقوله حَتَّى إِذا جاءَنا وقد قدمت أن الذي منع ذلك قد يكون اقتصر بمنعه على مجيء ذلك في جملة واحدة وأما إذا تعددت الجمل واستفلت كل بنفسها فقد لا يمنع ذلك حتى رددت على الزمخشري في قوله تعالى لا يَمْلِكُونَ الشَّفاعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمنِ عَهْداً فان الجملة واحدة، فانظره في موضعه.
Vol. 4, p. 251
1. (1) . “Earner and squanderer when you ask of him, he beams and shakes like the shaking of the Indian sword; and that is a man who, if he gives you a gift today with both his hands, will not prevent you from tomorrow’s gift. Whenever you come to him, you gaze dimly toward the light of his fire, you find the best of fires with the best of fuel-lighters.” By al-Ḥuṭayʾa. He says: he earns much and squanders much, and between the two is an antithesis (ṭibāq): when you ask him, he answers you quickly and with an open face, which is what is meant by “he beams and shakes like the shaking of a sword drawn out of Indian steel”; if he gives you a gift today with both hands — an allusion to the abundance of giving — and you ask him tomorrow, he gives you again. “ʿAshiya yaʿshā,” like “raḍiya yarḍā,” when his sight has an affliction; and “ʿashā yaʿshū” when he feigns dim sight without affliction. The meaning: whenever you come to him in the guise of the night-blind — figuratively, showing need — you find him the most generous of people; he expressed it so by way of allusion.
2. . “My fire and my neighbour’s fire are one, and my pot comes down to him before me; no neighbour whom I live beside harms me, [even] that his door should have no curtain. I look dimly aside whenever my neighbour-woman comes out, until her chamber-curtain covers my neighbour-woman.” By Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī. “ʿAshiya yaʿshā,” like “raḍiya yarḍā”: he became unable to see at night; and “ʿashā yaʿshū,” like “daʿā yadʿū”: when he looks like the look of the night-blind. He says: my fire is the fire of my neighbour, and my pot goes down to him so that he eats from it before me; or: my fire and my neighbour’s fire are one in time and strength, and nevertheless my pot goes down to him before me so that he eats it quickly, fearing that someone may see him. But it is unlikely, for the context is not to censure the neighbour but to praise. Then this is an allusion to the intensity of his generosity toward others; then he described himself with chastity by his saying: no neighbour of my neighbours has harmed me, by insult or otherwise, [even] that his door has no veil screening his family; for I feign unawareness and lower my gaze when my neighbour-woman comes out, until the chamber-curtain covers her. And he put the explicit noun in place of the pronoun to show that the right of neighbourliness must be observed. The first possibility is the sounder, because its meaning is that he treats him kindly and abstains from what is forbidden to him; as for the second, it contains censure of his neighbour, which does not suit what comes after it.
1. (1) . كسوب ومتلاف إذا ما سألته
…. تهلل واهتز اهتزاز المهند وذاك امرؤ إن يعطك اليوم نائلا
…. بكفيه لم يمنعك من نائل الغد متى تأته تعشو إلى ضوء ناره
…. تجد خير نار عندها خير موقد للحطيئة، يقول: هو كثير الكسب وكثير الإتلاف، وبينهما طباق التضاد: إذا سألته أجابك بسرعة وطلاقة وجه وهو المراد بقوله: تهلل واهتز كاهتزاز السيف المطلق من حديد الهند، إذا أعطاك اليوم عطاء بكفيه معا كناية عن كثرة العطاء، وسألته في غد أعطاك أيضا. وعشى يعشى كرضى يرضى: إذا كان ببصره آفة. وعشى يعشو: إذا تعاشى بغير آفة. والمعنى: منى تأته على هيئة الأعشى- مجاز عن إظهار الفاقة- تجده أكرم الناس، عبر عنه بذلك على طريق الكناية.
2. . ناري ونار الجار واحدة
…. وإليه قبلي تنزل القدر ما ضرني جار أجاوره
…. ألا يكون لبابه ستر أعشو إذا ما جارتى برزت
…. حتى يوارى جارتى الخدر لحاتم الطائي: وعشى يعشى كرضى يرضى: صار لا يبصر ليلا، وعشا يعشو كدعا يدعو: إذا نظر كنظر الأعشى. يقول: إن ناري هي نار جارى، وتنزل قدرى إليه ليأكل منها قبلي أو ناري ونار جارى واحدة في الزمن والقوة ومع ذلك تنزل قدره إليه قبلي ليأكلها سريعا خوف اطلاع أحد عليه. لكن يبعد هذا أن المقام ليس لذم الجار بل للمدح. ثم هذا كناية عن شدة كرمه على غيره، ثم وصف نفسه بالعفة بقوله: ما ضرني جار من جيراني بمسبة ولا غيرها من أن لا يكون لبابه حجاب يستر أهله، فانى أتغافل وأغض بصرى إذا خرجت جارتى، حتى يسترها بينها. وأتى بالظاهر موضع المضمر ليفيد أنه ينبغي مراعاة حق الجوار. والاحتمال الأول أقعد، لأن معناه أنه يبره ويعف عن محارمه. وأما الثاني ففيه ذم جاره، وهو لا يلائم بعده.
Vol. 4, p. 252
1. (1) . His saying “nuqayyiḍ lahu shayṭānan: nakhdhuluhu”: interpreting it so is based on that He, Most High, does not do the ugly, which is the Muʿtazila’s school. According to the people of the Sunna, He is the doer of all that exists, so the verses are on their apparent sense. (ʿ)
2. . His saying “idhā raʾā l-mamnuwwa bi-shidda”: i.e., the afflicted one. And “munia” means “he was afflicted.” As stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «نقيض له شيطانا: نخذله» تأويله بذلك مبنى على أنه تعالى لا يفعل القبيح، وهو مذهب المعتزلة. وعند أهل السنة أنه فاعل الكائنات كلها، فالآيات على ظاهرها (ع)
2. . قوله «إذا رأى الممنو بشدة» أى المبتلى. ومنى: أى ابتلى. أفاده الصحاح (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 253
1. (1) . “The rising of the sun reminds me of Ṣakhr, and I recall him at every sunset. And had it not been for the many weepers around me for their brothers, I would have killed myself. They do not weep like [for] my brother, but I console myself over him with consolation.” By al-Khansāʾ, lamenting her brother. Attributing the reminding to the rising is a rational figure (majāz ʿaqlī), because it is a cause of her remembering him; likewise the setting, since his going out was at the first and his return at the second, by custom; or because he went out at the first for raids and sat at the second with guests; or because its rising resembles his appearance and its setting resembles his death. In it is a type of badīʿ called “al-tankīt”: bringing a word that something else could fill its place, were it not for a point in it that gives preference to its being singled out for mention — otherwise singling it out would be a mistake, as in singling out the two times here. So stated al-Suyūṭī in Sharḥ ʿUqūd al-Jumān. And in it is another type called “al-idmāj”: that speech brought for one meaning includes within it another meaning, as the speech brought here for the meaning of lament includes the meaning of praise for courage and generosity, or for handsome appearance. And the bāʾ in “bi-kull” is causal. It is possible that the attribution for the first is of the type of attribution to time, so the bāʾ in the second would mean “in” or “with”; and mention of the sun a second time at the end of the second hemistich is of the type of “returning the end to the beginning.” “Aʿzī l-nafs”: I console it and make it patient about him with consolation (taʾassī), i.e., following the example of others among the afflicted; and in her following the men who weep is an indication of her fortitude and her standing among them. It is related “ʿalā amwātihim” in place of “ʿalā ikhwānihim,” and “usallī” in place of “aʿzī.”
2. . The explanation of this verse-witness was given in volume three, page 40; consult it if you wish. — The corrector. [.....]
1. (1) . يذكرني طلوع الشمس صخرا
…. وأذكره بكل غروب شمس ولولا كثرة الباكين حولي
…. على إخوانهم لقتلت نفسي وما يبكون مثل أخى ولكن
…. أعزى النفس عنه بالتأسى للخنساء ترثى أخاها. وإسناد التذكير الطلوع: مجاز عقلى، لأنه سبب في تذكيرها إياه، وكذلك الغروب حيث كان ذهابه عند الأول وإيابه عند الثاني عادة. أو لأنه يذهب في الأول للغارات، ويجلس في الثاني مع الضيفان. أو لأن طلوعها يشبه طلعته، وغروبها: يشبه موته. وفيه نوع من البديع يسمى التنكيت: وهو الإتيان بلفظ يسد غيره مسده، لولا نكتة فيه ترجح اختصاصه بالذكر: لكان اختصاصه خطأ، كما في اختصاص الوقتين هنا. أفاده السيوطي في شرح عقود الجمان. وفيه أيضا نوع آخر يسمى الادماج: وهو أن يضمن كلام سيق لمعنى معنى آخر، كما ضمن الكلام المسوق هنا لمعنى الرثاء معنى المدح بالشجاعة والكرم. أو بحسن الطلعة. والباء في «بكل» سببيه. ويحتمل أن الاسناد للأول من باب الاسناد للزمان، فتكون الباء في الثاني بمعنى «في» أو «مع» وذكر الشمس ثانيا في آخر المصراع الثاني من باب رد العجز على الصدر. وأعزى النفس: أسليها وأصبرها عنه بالتأسى، أى: الاقتداء بغيري من أهل المصائب وفي اقتدائها بالباكين من الرجال: إشعار بتجلدها وعظم شأنها مثلهم. وروى «على أمواتهم» بدل: «على إخوانهم» ، و «أسلى» بدل «أعزى» .
2. . مر شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الثالث صفحة 40 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه. [.....]

Q 43:40 · Vol. 4, p. 253

Verse 40

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Can you then make the deaf hear or guide the blind, and whoever is in clear error? (40)
أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ أَوْ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَمَنْ كانَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ (40)
Vol. 4, p. 253
The Messenger of God ﷺ used to strive, exert himself and toil with his soul in calling his people, while they did nothing but increase in firmness upon disbelief and persistence in error; so He rebuked him with His saying “Can you then make the deaf hear” — a denial of wonder that it should be he who is able to guide them, intending that none is able to do that for them except Him alone, by way of compulsion and force, as in His saying Most High “Indeed God makes hear whom He wills, and you are not one to make hear those in the graves.”
كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجد ويجتهد ويكدّ روحه في دعاء قومه، وهم لا يزيدون على دعائه إلا تصميما على الكفر وتماديا في الغىّ، فأنكر عليه بقوله أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ إنكار تعجيب من أن يكون هو الذي يقدر على هدايتهم، وأراد أنه لا يقدر على ذلك منهم إلا هو وحده على سبيل الإلجاء والقسر، كقوله تعالى إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُسْمِعُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَما أَنْتَ بِمُسْمِعٍ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 253

Q 43:41–43 · Vol. 4, pp. 253–254

Verses 41 to 43

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So whether We take you away, still We will take retribution from them (41) or We show you that which We promised them — for indeed, We are over them Powerful (42) So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path (43)
فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُمْ مُنْتَقِمُونَ (41) أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ الَّذِي وَعَدْناهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُقْتَدِرُونَ (42) فَاسْتَمْسِكْ بِالَّذِي أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (43)
Vol. 4, p. 254
“Mā” in His saying “fa-immā nadhhabanna bika” is in the position of the oath’s lām, in that when it enters, the emphatic nūn enters with it. The meaning: if We take you before We give you victory over them and heal the hearts of the believers from them, “indeed, We will take retribution from them” — the severest retribution in the Hereafter, as in His saying Most High “Or We cause you to die, and to Us they will be returned.” And if We wish to bring about in your lifetime what We promised them of punishment descending upon them — which is the Day of Badr — then they are under Our dominion and power; they cannot escape Us. He described them with hardness of resolve in disbelief and error, and then followed it with the severity of the threat of punishment in this world and the next. It is also read “nuriyannaka” with the light nūn. It is also read “bi-lladhī awḥā ilayka” with the verb active, the subject being God, Mighty and Exalted. The meaning: whether We hasten for you victory and triumph or delay it to the Last Day, be one who holds fast to what We revealed to you and to acting by it, for it is the straight path from which none deviates except an erring, wretched one; and increase each day in firmness in defending God’s religion, and let not weariness with their affair bring you to any softness or laxity in your matter, but [act] as the steadfast one does,(1) whom hastening of victory does not make eager and whose delay does not make hesitant.
«ما» في قوله فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ بمنزلة لام القسم: في أنها إذا دخلت دخلت معها النون المؤكدة، والمعنى: فإن قبضناك قبل أن ننصرك عليهم ونشفى صدور المؤمنين منهم فَإِنَّا مِنْهُمْ مُنْتَقِمُونَ أشد الانتقام في الآخرة، كقوله تعالى: أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيْنا يُرْجَعُونَ وإن أردنا أن ننجز في حياتك ما وعدناهم من العذاب النازل بهم وهو يوم بدر، فهم تحت ملكتنا وقدرتنا لا يفوتوننا: وصفهم بشدة الشكيمة في الكفر والضلال ثم أتبعه شدة الوعيد بعذاب الدنيا والآخرة. وقرئ: نرينك، بالنون الخفيفة. وقرئ: بالذي أوحى إليك، على البناء للفاعل، وهو الله عز وجل والمعنى: وسواء عجلنا لك الظفر والغلبة أو أخرنا إلى اليوم الآخر. فكن مستمسكا بما أوحينا إليك وبالعمل به فإنه الصراط المستقيم الذي لا يحيد عنه إلا ضال شقى، وزد كل يوم صلابة في المحاماة على دين الله، ولا يخرجك الضجر بأمرهم إلى شيء من اللين والرخاوة في أمرك، ولكن كما يفعل الثابت «1» الذي لا ينشطه تعجيل ظفر، ولا يثبطه تأخيره.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 253

1. (1) . His saying “wa-lākin kamā yafʿalu l-thābit”: perhaps “wa-kun,” or perhaps “wa-lākin kun.” (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “The asking of the messengers is figurative for examining their laws and looking into their creeds … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: And bearing witness to the intention of asking the communities is “So ask those who have been reading the Book before you.” And God knows best.

Q 43:44–45 · Vol. 4, pp. 254–255

Verses 44 to 45

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And indeed, it is a remembrance for you and your people, and you will be questioned (44) And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Have We made besides the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped? (45)
وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ وَسَوْفَ تُسْئَلُونَ (44) وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنا أَجَعَلْنا مِنْ دُونِ الرَّحْمنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ (45)
Vol. 4, p. 254
“And indeed it”: and indeed that which has been revealed to you is “a remembrance,” an honour, “for you and your people, and you will be questioned” about it on the Day of Resurrection, and about your fulfilment of its right, your magnifying it, and your gratitude that you were given it and singled out for it among all the worlds. The asking of the messengers is not meant as real asking, because it is impossible, but is figurative for looking into their religions and examining their creeds: did the worship of idols ever come in any of the creeds of the prophets? It suffices as looking and examining(2) that he looks into God’s inimitable Book, which confirms what is before it, and God’s informing in it that they worship besides God that for which He sent down no authority. This verse in itself is sufficient, with no need of another. And the asking that occurs figuratively for looking, where asking in reality is not valid, is much; of it is the poets’ questioning the abodes, the traces and the ruins; and the saying of one who said: “Ask the earth: who cut your rivers, planted your trees and gathered your fruits? For if it does not answer you in speech,(3) it will answer you in lesson.” It was said to him [i.e., the Prophet]: the prophets were gathered for him on the Night of the Ascent in Jerusalem, and he led them in prayer. And it was said to him: ask them — and he did not doubt and did not ask. It is also said: its meaning is: ask the communities of those We sent, who are the People of the two Books, the Torah and the Gospel. And from
وَإِنَّهُ وإنّ الذي أوحى إليك لَذِكْرٌ لشرف لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ، وَلسوف تُسْئَلُونَ عنه يوم القيامة، وعن قيامكم بحقه، وعن تعظيمكم له، وشكركم على أن رزقتموه وخصصتم به من بين العالمين، ليس المراد بسؤال الرسل حقيقة السؤال لإحالته، ولكنه مجاز عن النظر في أديانهم والفحص عن مللهم، هل جاءت عبادة الأوثان قط في ملة من ملل الأنبياء؟ وكفاه نظرا وفحصا «2» : نظره في كتاب الله المعجز المصدّق لما بين يديه، وإخبار الله فيه بأنهم يعبدون من دون الله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا. وهذه الآية في نفسها كافية لا حاجة إلى غيرها، والسؤال الواقع مجازا عن النظر، حيث لا يصح السؤال على الحقيقة: كثير منه مساءلة الشعراء الديار والرسوم والأطلال. وقول من قال: سل الأرض من شق أنهارك وغرس أشجارك وجنى ثمارك؟ فإنها إن لم تجبك حوارا «3» أجابتك اعتبارا. وقيل له: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جمع له الأنبياء ليلة الإسراء في بيت المقدس فأمّهم. وقيل له: سلهم، فلم يشكك ولم يسأل. وقيل: معناه سل أمم من أرسلنا وهم أهل الكتابين: التوراة والإنجيل. وعن
Vol. 4, p. 255
al-Farrāʾ: they only inform him about the books of the messengers, so when he asks them it is as though he asked the prophets.
الفراء: هم إنما يخبرونه عن كتب الرسل، فإذا سألهم فكأنه سأل الأنبياء.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 254
1. (1) . His saying “wa-lākin kamā yafʿalu l-thābit”: perhaps “wa-kun,” or perhaps “wa-lākin kun.” (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “The asking of the messengers is figurative for examining their laws and looking into their creeds … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: And bearing witness to the intention of asking the communities is “So ask those who have been reading the Book before you.” And God knows best.
3. . His saying “tujibka ḥiwāran”: i.e., addressing in speech. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: istaḥārahu, i.e., made him speak. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «ولكن كما يفعل الثابت» لعله: وكن. أو لعله: ولكن كن. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «سؤال الرسل مجاز عن الفحص في شرائعهم والنظر في مللهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: ويشهد لارادة سؤال الأمم فَسْئَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُنَ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ والله أعلم.
3. . قوله «تجبك حوارا» أى مخاطبة بالنطق. في الصحاح: استحاره، أى: استنطقه. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 255
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “It is permissible to answer ‘lammā’ with the ‘idhā’ of suddenness because the verb of suddenness is estimated with it and is what governs it in the accusative … etc.” Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: The apparent justification of this wording — and God knows best — is that each one of these verses, when you consider it by itself, its greatness absorbs the mind and dazzles it, until one is certain that it is the ultimate and every other sign is below it; and when the mind moves to its sister, its greatness likewise fills his mind and he forgets the first and is certain that this is the ultimate and every other sign is below it. In sum, the mind cannot combine two of them so as to verify which is the superior and which is the inferior; rather, whenever it takes one alone, it is certain that it is the ultimate. And on this estimate runs everything of its kind that occurs; and God knows best.
2. . His saying “idhā qarawtahum rajulan rajulan”: i.e., you followed them one by one. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «جازت فيه إجابة لما بإذا التي المفاجأة لأن فعل المفاجأة مقدر معها وهو العامل فيها النصب
…. الخ» قال أحمد: الظاهر في تسويغ هذا الإطلاق- والله أعلم: أن كل واحدة من هذه الآي إذا أفردتها بالفكر استغرقت عظمتها الفكر وبهرته، حتى يجزم أنها النهاية، وأن كل آية دونها. فإذا نقل الفكرة إلى أختها استوعيت أيضا فكره بعظمها، وذهل عن الأولى فجزم بأن هذه النهاية، وأن كل آية دونها. والحاصل أنه لا يقدر الفكر على أن يجمع بين آيتين منهما، ليتحقق عنده الفاضلة من المفضولة، بل مهما أفرده بالكفر جزم بأنه النهاية. وعلى هذا التقدير يجرى جميع ما يرد من أمثاله، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «إذا قروتهم رجلا رجلا» أى تتبعتهم. (ع)

Q 43:46–47 · Vol. 4, p. 255

Verses 46 to 47

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, and he said, “Indeed, I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds” (46) But when he brought them Our signs, at once they were laughing at them (47)
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلائِهِ فَقالَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (46) فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِآياتِنا إِذا هُمْ مِنْها يَضْحَكُونَ (47)
Vol. 4, p. 255
What they answered him with, at his saying “Indeed I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds,” is omitted, indicated by His saying “But when he brought them Our signs”: it is their demanding of him to produce proof for his claim and to display the sign. “At once they were laughing at them”: i.e., they mocked them and ridiculed them and called them sorcery; and “idhā” is for suddenness.
ما أجابوه به عند قوله: إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ محذوف، دل عليه قوله: فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِآياتِنا وهو مطالبتهم إياه بإحضار البينة على دعواه وإبراز الآية إِذا هُمْ مِنْها يَضْحَكُونَ أى يسخرون منها ويهزءون بها ويسمونها سحرا، وإذا للمفاجأة.
Question
If you say: how is it permissible for “lammā” to be answered by the sudden “idhā”?
فإن قلت: كيف جاز أن يجاب لما بإذا المفاجأة؟
Answer
I say: because the verb of suddenness is estimated with it, and it is what governs the accusative(1) in its position, as if it were said: “when he brought them Our signs, they suddenly [burst into] their laughing time.”
قلت: لأنّ فعل المفاجأة معها مقدّر. وهو عامل النصب «1» في محلها، كأنه قيل: فلما جاءهم بآياتنا فاجئوا وقت ضحكهم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 255
